key_points: Housing guaranteed freshman year only; off-campus costs are brutal.
Miami/Coral Gables rental market is extremely expensive.
Standard dorm rules apply, including appliance restrictions.
Greek life is active and generally welcoming to international students.
Some business fraternities exclude lower-income students via expensive trips.
Sorority recruitment can be intimidating and opaque for internationals.
No meaningful student feedback exists on campus dining quality.
Students focus on Miami's restaurant scene over dining halls.
Dining quality remains effectively unrated and undiscussed.
Academic pressure and financial stress drive notable mental health struggles.
One student hid a mental health crisis from their parents.
No clear student feedback on UM's mental health services.
UM is stingy with aid, especially for international students.
Average international merit package is ~$25k; far from full cost.
Aid appeals are possible but slow and documentation-heavy.
90% of advisors described as unhelpful by one student.
The cognate gen-ed system confuses many incoming students.
Pre-med students debate grade difficulty versus research access at UM.
Waitlist and transfer decisions drag slowly, sometimes into July.
Students confused by basic portals and login systems.
Financial aid processing is lengthy and bureaucratically inefficient.
Coral Gables campus is consistently praised as beautiful and well-designed.
A car is needed to access much of Miami properly.
Metrorail to Brickell is a practical, affordable commuting option.
UM's name recognition is solid but not exceptional in most fields.
Music and entertainment careers launch better from NYC than Miami.
Career center gets generic mentions with no standout praise.
UM is widely seen as overpriced vs. comparable Florida schools.
FIU and USF offer similar pre-med quality at far lower cost.
Only worth full price with significant merit aid or wealth.
UM has a wealthy, image-conscious 'sun and money' social culture.
Campus is genuinely beautiful and students are proud of it.
'Harvard of the South' label reflects self-perception over academic reality.
Cost: Off-campus housing and Miami lifestyle are financially punishing.
Financial Aid: Limited support leaves internationals significantly underfunded.
Academics: Grade deflation threatens pre-med GPAs and med school prospects.
Students get Coral Gables resident rates at the Biltmore Golf Course.
Library loans camera equipment, a valuable perk for creative students.
Metrorail makes Brickell and downtown Miami surprisingly cheap to access.
